subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base session rows immediately on `cron.remove`, or should orphaned base rows be removed only through guarded retention cleanup?
rationale: Current main still leaves the rows, while related PR discussion shows live base rows preserve user model/auth/label choices, so the permanent cleanup boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Guarded retention cleanup
options.body: Use the member-authored orphan-only retention path so deleted-job base rows are cleaned after the retention window while live job-owned rows stay protected.

options.title: Immediate delete cleanup
options.body: Clean the deleted job's base and run session rows during `cron.remove`, with tests proving active-run and per-agent store behavior are safe.

options.title: Split the scopes
options.body: Land guarded retention first and track immediate Control UI ghost-session cleanup as a narrower follow-up if the delayed cleanup is not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Guarded retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Use the member-authored orphan-only retention path so deleted-job base rows are cleaned after the retention window while live job-owned rows stay protected.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the open member PR that documents and implements the guarded orphan-cleanup boundary.
